why: Counting set bits for every number at once: i >> 1 is a smaller number already done, and i & 1 is the bit you dropped, so bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1) fills the table in O(n).
hints: Counting bits of each number separately costs O(n log n). Can each answer reuse an earlier one?
Shifting i right by one drops its last bit. How do the bit counts of i and i >> 1 differ?
res = [0]*(n+1); for i in 1..n: res[i] = res[i >> 1] + (i & 1). (Or res[i] = res[i & (i-1)] + 1.)
pitfalls: The output has n + 1 entries, from 0 through n.
